editorial:
Imagine getting lost in a massive, beautiful forest in Ireland and finding a strange shelter where three strangers are already hiding. That is the setup for this fantasy horror mystery. You follow a young artist who ends up trapped with these people, and every night, mysterious creatures watch them through a one-way mirror. The vibe is tense and eerie, with a slow burn that keeps you guessing about what is really going on. The forest feels alive, and the shelter becomes a cage you cannot escape.

The acting is solid, especially from the lead, who carries the fear and confusion well. The pacing starts slow but picks up as secrets come out. The creature design is creepy, though the story can feel a bit confusing at times. If you enjoy mystery horror with a twist, this is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn the creatures are actually shape-shifters who have been copying humans. The shelter was built by a scientist who studied them. The artist discovers she has a special connection to the creatures and can control them. She escapes the forest with one of the strangers, but the twist reveals the creatures are now free and spreading into the human world. The final shot shows one of them watching from the trees, hinting the nightmare is far from over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves atmospheric horror with a twist ending.
